en.title: Active and passive voice
en.summary: In the active the subject acts; in the passive the subject receives the action.

paragraphs: Voice shows the relation between the verb and its subject. In an active sentence, the subject does the action. In a passive sentence, the subject is the person or thing the action happens to, and the doer is either left out or introduced with by.

items: The meal **was cooked** by the chef. (passive)
The meal **was cooked**. (the doer is not mentioned)

paragraphs: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence. The verb takes a passive form, and the old subject, if kept, appears after by.

blocks.html:
ActivePassive
Shakespeare wrote the play.The play was written by Shakespeare.
People speak English here.English is spoken here.
Someone has stolen my bike.My bike has been stolen.
They will announce the result.The result will be announced.

paragraphs: The passive lets the speaker put the focus on the object or the result, and it is the natural choice when the doer is unknown, unimportant or too obvious to mention. It is very common in news, science and formal writing.

blocks.html:
PurposeExample
doer unknownMy car was stolen.
doer unimportantThe road is being repaired.
focus on the resultThe window was broken by a ball.
formal toneYou are requested to wait.

sections.title: Only some verbs have a passive

paragraphs: Only transitive verbs, which take an object, can be passive. Intransitive verbs such as arrive, sleep and happen have no passive: Something happened (not: It was happened).

items: Wrong: **The accident was happened yesterday.** Right: **The accident happened yesterday.**
Wrong: **English speaks here.** Right: **English is spoken here.**
Wrong: **The book was written from Orwell.** Right: **by Orwell**
